newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba to retain policy reins until Euro launched.
newsitem.headline: Buba to retain policy reins until Euro launched.

text.p: The Bundesbank will continue to guide monetary policy until it passes over its policy-making capacity to the European central bank after currency union is launched, the bank's vice president said on Thursday.

"We will continue to be able to act and all those who think that the Bundesbank will no longer be able to act are wrong," Johann Wilhelm Gaddum told German television on the eve of the central bank's 40th birthday.
Gaddum brushed aside speculation that the Bundesbank would turn into a lame duck central bank, unable to make policies, in the run-up to Europe's monetary union, scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999
He also stressed that independence and public trust were the two fundamental assets of the Bundesbank, both influential in keeping the mark stable and strong.
"Trust is the most important capital which we have," Gaddum said.
